## Plan

### Mechanics summary
- 252 HP `[GAME-EXTRACT]`.
- Moves `[GAME-EXTRACT]`:
  - Stamp: gains **150 Plow**
  - Plow: 18 + 2 Strength
  - Stun
  - Beast Cry: Ringing on your cards
  - Stomp: 15
  - Crush: 17 + 3 Strength
- **The wiki confirms the modelled cycle** `[COMMUNITY]` (slaythespire.wiki.gg page, accessed 2026-11-19): Stamp (150 Plow, 160 at A9), Plow 18 (20) + 2 Strength every turn until HP reaches the Plow amount, stun (Strength lost), then Beast Cry (Ringing: one card), Stomp 15 (17), Crush 17 (19) + 3 (4) Strength; HP 252 (262 at A8+). So the simulator's failure here is not the cycle; real decks' strength is the likelier cause.
- **Plow** `[GAME-EXTRACT]`: after taking damage, it removes the Beast's Strength and stuns it, then the power goes away. The 150 is presumably a damage threshold `[HYPOTHESIS]`.
- **Community guides (search summaries, 2026-11-19):** Plow triggers when the Beast's HP drops to **150** (not after 150 damage; 150–160 at higher ascension), stunning it and wiping its Strength. In phase two, Beast Cry's **Ringing lets you play only one card on your next turn**. Guides advise bringing it to about 150 right before Beast Cry, and not entering phase two with too much HP left `[COMMUNITY]`.
- A first simulation with the other reading (Plow 18 + 2 Strength every turn until 150 HP is lost) makes the fight far harder than the Player's record (2% simulated wins against 5 of 6 real survivals; `reports/phase2/vantom-simulation.md`), so at least one assumption is wrong: Plow may not be a 150-HP threshold, or the Beast may not Plow every turn. With the 150-HP threshold the model is still too hard (9%). Changing one assumption at a time (`tools/simulate_fight.py --beast-sensitivity`): no Strength on Plow 77%, Plow 12 damage 72%, no Ringing limit 37%, two-turn stun 36%, threshold 180 HP 15%. Read Plow's intent each turn, the Ringing effect and the stun length in the first fight (gap 25). A further search (2026-11-19) found more guides agreeing that Ringing allows one card on the next turn, and one saying Beast Cry then alternates with attacks; both point to a harder fight, so Plow's damage or Strength gain (or simply stronger real decks) is the likelier error. Read the intents and the Plow counter in the first fight.

### Deck checklist
- **Countable checks** (`tools/deck_check.py`, tuned on the history 2026-11-19) `[PLAYER-DATA, weak]`: Vulnerable sources at least 1 (front-load 150 damage to trigger Plow; survived 1.2, fatal 0.5).
- **Front-loaded damage** to break Plow quickly: about 150 damage over the first 3 turns. That resets its Strength and wins a stun turn.
- **Block about 18 per turn** early, rising with Strength.

### HP target on arrival
- Ironclad benchmark: median 39, p75 45.5. **Rest if HP is below about 49.** Fatal fights started lower (43% against 53%, all characters).

### First three turns
1. Stamp (gains Plow): free damage turn. Go all in.
2. Plow (18 + 2 Strength): block, keep attacking.
3. Keep pushing damage until Plow breaks; then use the stun turn to set up.

### Potion plan
- Strength and attack potions early to break Plow.

### What killed the Player here, and the counter
- Ironclad: 1 of 7 fatal (all characters: 6 of 32). `[PLAYER-DATA]`
- Counter: break Plow early; don't let its Strength stack.
